blindWork: Initial HCl = 50.0 mL x 0.100 M = 5.00 mmol; NaOH back-titrant = 6.2 mL x 0.150 M = 0.93 mmol, so HCl consumed by carbonate = 4.07 mmol. CaCO3 + 2HCl, so n(CaCO3) = 2.035 mmol = 0.2037 g. % = 0.2037/0.500 x 100 = 40.7% (approximately 41%, allowing for the 2-s.f. titrant volume).
stem: Acid-Base Titration (Back Titration): A $0.500\text{-g}$ antacid tablet containing $\text{CaCO}_{3}$ was treated with $50.0\text{~mL}$ of $0.100\text{~M~HCl}$. The excess acid required $6.2\text{~mL}$ of $0.150\text{~M~NaOH}$ for complete neutralization. What percentage by mass of the tablet is $\text{CaCO}_{3}$? ($\text{CaCO}_{3} = 100.09\text{~g/mol}$)
sourceExplanation: Total acid = $0.050 \times 0.100 = 0.005\text{~mol}$. Excess $\text{NaOH}$ neutralized excess acid: $n\left( \text{NaOH} \right) = 0.0062 \times 0.150 = 0.00093\text{~mol}$. Acid reacted with $\text{CaCO}_{3} = 0.005 - 0.00093 = 0.00407\text{~mol}$. Moles $\text{CaCO}_{3} = 0.002035\text{~mol}$. Mass $= 0.002035 \times 100.09 = 0.2037\text{~g}$. $\% = (0.2037/0.500) \times 100\% = 40.7\% \approx$ let's re-verify titration stoichiometry: $2\text{HCl} + \text{CaCO}_{3}$. (C)
